Petition under Section 166 & 140 of M.V. Act, 1988 for grant of compensation Award
1.

The present petition has been filed U/s 166 & 140 M.V.Act seeking compensation of Rs.
70,00,000/- alongwith interest @ 18% per annum from the date of filing of the present claim petition till its realization on account of injuries suffered by petitioner Sh. Rakesh Singh @ Rajender Singh (aged 25 years) in road traffic accident in question which occurred on 02.01.2014.

The concise material facts relevant to decide the present claim petition as averred are that on 02.01.2014, injured Rakesh Singh @ Rajender Singh alongwith Sandeep Singh (injured in other case bearing MACP No. 457/19) were coming to their house on motorcycle, on the correct side of the road at normal speed.

At about 11:50 PM, when they reached near Krishi Sewa Kendra Orai Jaloun Road Bahad Gram Ruramallu, UP, in the meantime, a vehicle no. UP79T-1154 which was being driven by its driver at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, came from the side of Orai and hit against the aforesaid motorcycle on which petitioner was travelling, as a result of which,
both the riders of motorcycle fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.

He was immediately taken to Government Hospital, Jaloun, UP from the place of accident and thereafter,
he was referred to Kanpur Hospital, UP.
A case U/s 279/338/427 IPC & 184 M.V. Act was registered at PS. Kotwali, District Jaloun, UP vide FIR No. 25/14 with regard to the accident in question.
The petitioner has claimed that the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of aforementioned offending vehicle which was allegedly being driven by respondent no.4/driver.

The offending vehicle was found to be possessed by respondent no. 2, owned by respondent no. 3 and was duly insured with respondent no. 1/National Insurance Co. Ltd., at the time of accident in question.
3. In its written statement, the respondent no. 1/insurance company has not raised any statutory defence as provided u/s. 149(2) M.V. Act.

14. There is no merit in the contention raised on behalf of respondent no. 1 that testimony of PW1 is liable to be discarded on the ground that FIR in the present case was registered on 01.02.2014 i.e.
after about 29 days from the date of accident.
No doubt, accident had occurred on 02.01.2014 and FIR in the present case, was registered on 01.02.2014 i.e. after about 29 days from the date of accident.
However, the petitioner has furnished explanation for delay in lodging the FIR in his statement itself, which led to the registration of the FIR.

The contents of FIR would show that the petitioner clearly mentioned therein the reason for delay in lodging of FIR that he could not get the FIR lodged on time as he was not in position to give statement due to grievous injuries suffered by him in the accident in question.
It may be noted here that petitioner has relied upon copy of chargesheet as Ex. PW1/4.
Even otherwise, Ld. Counsel for insurance company has not disputed his presence at the time of accident.
Rather, she had given the suggestion to the petitioner that accident in question had occurred due to his negligence.
It is relevant to note that respondent no. 1 did not cross-examine PW1 regarding the explanation for delay in registration of FIR.
Moreover, the MLC of the petitioner/injured is of 03.01.2014(accident being caused on 02.01.2014 at about 11:50 pm) at about 00:35 hrs showing therein alleged history of RTA.

Apart from this, Ld. Counsel for insurance company himself gave suggestion to the petitioner that the accident had taken place due to sole negligence of his friend Sh.
Rakesh which shows that insurance company admitted the accident and involvement of offending vehicle in the accident in question.

16. In the aforesaid facts and circumstances where the cogent explanation has been furnished about the delay in the registration of FIR in criminal case, same can not be considered to be fatal for the case of claimant in present proceedings.

Even otherwise, it is well settled law that delay in lodging FIR can not be a ground to throw away the case of claimant in such like proceedings in the backdrop of the conditions prevailing in our society where one can not expect common man to rush to police station for registration of FIR immediately after the accident.
While saying so, I am fortified by the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the matter titled as "Ravi Vs. Badri Narayan & Ors.", Civil Appeal No. 1926/2011, decided on 18.02.2011.

18. Section 168 of the Motor Vehicle Act 1988 enjoins upon the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.

19. It has been duly established that petitioner sustained injuries in the road accident which took place on 02.01.2014 at 11:50 pm at Krishi Sewa Kendra Orai Jaloun Road Bahad Gram Ruramallu,
UP, as per his MLC and treatment record duly proved, in the said road traffic accident due to rash and negligent driving of the respondent no. 4/driver.

The intent and objective of the Beneficial Legislation is to grant equitable compensation to the vulnerable victims of road accidents and dynamic law has evolved towards grant of just and fair quantum of awards MACP No. 456/19; FIR No. 25/14 DOD: 10.02.2025 and has brought consistency and uniformity towards the desired goal.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in "Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation" (2009) 6 SCC 121, which was affirmed by a bench of three Honble Judges in Reshma Kumari & Ors. Vs.

held as under:
"16.

"Just compensation" is adequate compensation which is fair and equitable, on the facts and circumstances of the case, to make good the loss suffered as a result of the wrong, as far as money can do so, by applying the well settled principles relating to award of compensation.
It is not intended to be a bonanza, largesse or source of profit.
17. Assessment of compensation though involving certain hypothetical considerations, should nevertheless be objective.
Justice and justness emanate from equality in treatment, consistency and thoroughness in adjudication, and fairness and uniformity in the decision making process and the decisions.
While it may not be possible to have mathematical precision or identical awards, in assessing compensation, same or similar facts should lead to awards in the same range.

When the factors/inputs are the same, and the formula/legal principles are the same,
consistency and uniformity, and not divergence and freakiness, should be the result of adjudication to arrive at just compensation..."

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by the respondent no. 4.
Reliance placed on Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Co. Ltd. V.
Kamlesh & Ors, MAC APP. No. 530/2008 passed by Hon'ble Delhi High Court on 11.11.2008.
No doubt, accident had occurred on 02.01.2014 and FIR in the present case, was registered on 01.02.2014 i.e. after about 29 days from the date of accident.
However, the petitioner has furnished explanation for delay in lodging the FIR in his statement itself, which led to the registration of the FIR.
The contents of FIR would show that the petitioner clearly mentioned therein the reason for delay in lodging of FIR that he could not get the FIR lodged on time as he was not in position to give statement due to grievous injuries suffered by him in the accident in question.
16. In the aforesaid facts and circumstances where the cogent explanation has been furnished about the delay in the registration of FIR in criminal case, same can not be considered to be fatal for the case of claimant in present proceedings.
Even otherwise, it is well settled law that delay in lodging FIR can not be a ground to throw away the case of claimant in such like proceedings in the backdrop of the conditions prevailing in our society where one can not expect common man to rush to police station for registration of FIR immediately after the accident.
19. It has been duly established that petitioner sustained injuries in the road accident which took place on 02.01.2014 at 11:50 pm at Krishi Sewa Kendra Orai Jaloun Road Bahad Gram Ruramallu,
UP, as per his MLC and treatment record duly proved, in the said road traffic accident due to rash and negligent driving of the respondent no. 4/driver.
20.
The intent and objective of the Beneficial Legislation is to grant equitable compensation to the vulnerable victims of road accidents and dynamic law has evolved towards grant of just and fair quantum of awards MACP No. 456/19; FIR No. 25/14 DOD: 10.02.2025 and has brought consistency and uniformity towards the desired goal.
The Hon'ble Apex Court in "Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation" (2009) 6 SCC 121, which was affirmed by a bench of three Honble Judges in Reshma Kumari & Ors. Vs.
Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65,
Rakesh Singh @ Rajender Singh vs National Insurance Co on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133382712/
6 21.
The Hon'ble Apex Court, in further development of the legal position for grant of reasonable and fair compensation, has pronounced guiding parameters that "the compensation should be just and is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be niggardly or a pittance".
Reliance is placed on 2012 (8) SLT 676 titled K. Suresh Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
In the absence of any definite evidence being brought on record showing the actual period till which the petitioner had received medical treatment for the injuries sustained by him due to accident in question, it would necessarily involve some guess in assessing the loss of income.
It can not be overlooked that the petitioner had sustained polytrauma with facial head injury with fracture of femur shaft(right) and fracture patella(right)as mentioned above due to the accident.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, it is presumed that he would not have been able to work atleast for a period of 6 months or so.
Petitioner has also failed to file his educational qualification documents.
Thus, his loss of income has to be assessed while taking the income of an unskilled person under Minimum Wages Act MACP No. 456/19; FIR No. 25/14 DOD:
10.02.2025 applicable during the period in question.
It is settled law that a particular amount cannot be fixed on pain and sufferings for all cases as is varies from case to case.
Judicial notice can be taken on the fact that since the petitioner had got injuries/fracture as aforesaid, he mighthave suffered acute pain and sufferings owing to the said injuries.
Thus, he would have undergone great physical sufferings,
inconvenience and mental trauma on account of the accident in question.
Keeping in view the nature of injuries suffered by the petitioner and duration of treatment, a sum of Rs. 50,000/- is considered reasonable towards pain & sufferings.
LOSS OF GENERAL AMENITIES & ENJOYMENT OF LIFE 32.
As already mentioned above, there is sufficient evidence on record to establish that the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
Thus, he would not be able to enjoy general amenities of life after the accident in question and his quality of life has been definitely affected.
In view of the nature of injuries suffered by him and his continued treatment for considerable period, I award a notional sum of Rs. 50,000/- towards loss of general amenities and enjoyment of life to the petitioner.
